Hallways need 36" minimum width per R311.6. On A2.01A, the south hallway (room 05) appears undimensioned for width.

**Issue found:** Hallway widths not dimensioned to confirm 36" minimum.

**Issue found:** Ceiling heights undimensioned, particularly at sloped ceiling areas.

Toilet clearances under R307.1/P2705.1 require 15" from centerline to obstructions and 21" clear space in front. Checking A7.02 elevations and A2.01A/B plans, toilet locations are shown but clearances aren't called out. The powder room (room 14) is notably tight at roughly 4'-6" × 3'-9"—clearances there deserve scrutiny.

**Issue found:** Toilet clearances not dimensioned to confirm code compliance.

Shower minimum interior dimension is 30" × 30" per R307.2. Checking A7.02 elevations for shower sizing next.

and dwelling requires 1/2" gypsum on the garage side, no openings, and a self-closing solid door at least 1-3/8" thick.

Door 15-1 is the 18' overhead garage door. There should also be a personnel door between garage and house—checking A2.01B, door 16-2 connects the garage to the north hallway, but its schedule lists it as an "Interior" door at 2'-6" × 7'-0" without specifying fire-rating or solid-core construction.

**Issue:** Door 16-2 is likely the garage-to-house fire separation door but the schedule doesn't specify a fire-rated door, self-closing hardware, or 1-3/8" solid core—all IRC requirements for this separation.

**Bathroom ventilation:** IRC R303.3 requires window or mechanical exhaust. Master bath, hall bath, and powder room all appear to have windows plus exhaust fans per specs—compliant.

**Smoke alarms:** IRC R314.3 mandates smoke alarms in each sleeping room, outside sleeping areas, and each story. Specs mention "smoke detection and carbon monoxide detection systems" but the reflected ceiling plan A6.01 doesn't show any smoke alarm locations, and neither does it show bathroom fan locations mentioned in specs (Broan Energy Star units)—both missing from RCP.

Deck detail 6/A5.30 defers to "SEE STRUCTURAL SET FOR DECK STRUCTURE" for the connection, which is appropriate for structural fastening, but architectural should still coordinate to show ledger location and flashing at the attachment point.

**Accessibility:** Not code-mandated for single-family homes unless owner-specified, but I see grab bars called out in the master bath shower (6/A7.02: "SIDE GRAB BARS" and "CORNER GRAB BARS") and bathroom 11 (2/A7.02: "CORNER GRAB BARS"), suggesting some accessibility consideration was intended.

**Tempered glass at tubs:** IRC R308.4.5 requires safety glazing near hot tubs/bathtubs within 60" horizontally and below 60" vertically of the water's edge. Bathroom elevations show windows near tubs/showers but don't specify tempered glass - this is a code gap worth flagging.

That covers the major code/life safety issues visible in the architectural set. Moving to Category F - Constructability, starting with the entry hall ceiling detail.

Detail 7/A4.10 shows a sloped roof over the entry hall with WD-4 T&G ceiling below, but the attachment method isn't clear - whether the T&G follows the roof slope directly or sits flat with a triangular attic space above needing its own detailing. Flagging this as unresolved.

Next, checking corner window jamb details on A4.13 - reading nook, kitchen, and office conditions each have their own detail, starting with 1/A4.13 for the reading nook.

This shows two window frames meeting at an outside corner with WD-1 wood veneer trim, weather barrier, and double 2x4 fiber cement trim with fiberboard corners. The exterior finish is documented, but there's no structural corner post or header support shown for how the two window assemblies are actually held up at the corner. Another gap to note.

Moving to the reading nook section, 1/A7.10, which shows a built-in bunk bed with ladder and shelving - labeled simply "framing as needed" without further specifics.

That's not sufficient for construction documents given the safety implications of bunk bed structures. Same issue I flagged earlier.

Checking the roof plan's complex ridges and valleys, standing seam metal typically needs custom-formed ridge caps, but neither R-1 assembly detail nor the eave detail (4/A4.11) address ridge or valley conditions - another missing detail.

Then there's the rain chain spec, which reads:

Downspouts - Japanese "rain chain" connect gutter drain to collection pots at grade." Rain chains need specific outlet fittings and base drainage, but elevations only note "GUTTER & RAIN CHAIN" without showing either connection point. Flagging this as another missing detail.

Moving to corner trim - detail 5/A4.10 specifies double 2x4 fiber cement boards with weather barrier and wood veneer, outside corners condition.

Sequencing isn't clear though: trim first then siding, or siding then trim? This matters for weatherproofing.

For the pool deck, A5.01/A5.20 defer structure to the structural set, which is fine, but detail 1/A5.30 mentions tapering the structure at landscape edges without explaining how the framing actually achieves that taper - another coordination gap worth noting.

Looking at the porch roof, detail 7/A4.10 shows LVL overhang framing, and the specs call out steel columns hidden inside the wall framing supporting it. But these column locations don't appear anywhere on the architectural plans or details - a "SEE STRUCTURAL" reference or indicated column locations would help.

Checking A2.01A and the island elevation on A7.01, the sink appears near the dishwasher (A2) on the island, but there's no indication of how supply/drain lines get routed under the floor to reach it - no plumbing chase shown on the floor plan.

Appliance clearances also aren't dimensioned: range door swing, fridge door swing/ventilation - detail 1/A7.01 shows a tight cabinet/appliance/pantry layout but no verification these clearances work.

For attic access, IRC R807.1 requires a 22"×30" opening when attic height >30" and area >30 SF. Room 20 on A2.02/A6.01 is labeled "Attic" but I don't see an access hatch called out.

Checking A2.01B, room 20 (Attic) has door 20-1, so access appears to be via door rather than hatch. The door schedule shows 3'-0"×7'-0" solid-core wood, which exceeds the minimum, so this satisfies code - retracting that issue.

For crawl space access, IRC R408.4 requires minimum 18"×24". Door 21-1 is 5'-0"×5'-0", well above minimum - compliant.

For laundry (room 12), plans label "WASHER" and "DRYER" locations but don't dimension the utility connections needed. The washer requires water supply, drain, and electrical; the dryer needs electrical and exhaust venting. A2.01B only notes closet shelf height, not these plumbing/electrical hookups - flagging as a potential gap in documentation.

For shower curbs, barrier-free showers max out at 1/2" per IRC, while standard curbs (typically 4-6") have no code max. Detail 6 on A7.02 ("MASTER BATHROOM 07 - SHOWER EAST") doesn't dimension curb height - another documentation gap.

Checking pool equipment access next - the mechanical area appears on A2.00 and A5.01 behind a wood fence enclosure, need to verify maintenance access clearances.

For a person to work on the equipment, gate width and interior clearances matter but aren't dimensioned anywhere in the plans. That's a real gap - **pool mechanical area access dimensions not shown**.

Moving to solar readiness - A2.03 shows "SOLAR ARRAY" on the garage roof, and specs mention making the system "solar ready" for PV. But there's no mounting system, roof penetration, or flashing detail shown for the standing seam roof. While electrical drawings might cover wiring, the roof penetration/waterproofing is architectural scope. **Issue: solar mounting and roof penetration details missing from architectural set.**

ration:**

A1.01 shows the LP gas line running from the buried tank to the house, but I don't see where it penetrates the foundation or crawl space wall - it presumably enters near the furnace, but that's not called out. **Issue: LP gas line foundation entry point not specifically indicated.**

That covers the major constructability issues - moving on to completeness and clarity now, checking for missing info, vague notes, TBD items, and inconsistencies.

Starting with door hardware: most schedule entries just show "---" with no specific hardware sets assigned, even though specs mention black metal door levers generally.

**Issue: Door schedule missing hardware specifications on most doors.**

The window schedule also has gaps - it lists type, size, material, and frame, but omits sill/head heights, rough openings, egress designation, and tempered glass requirements.

**Issue: Window schedule missing critical dimensional and safety information.**

Countertop thickness is another TBD item - specs list Silestone with "thickness TBD," while the kitchen elevation calls out backsplash as SS-1 6mm.

**Issue: Countertop thickness left unspecified.**

Paint colors also show as TBD in several places, like the Sherwin Williams lap siding color - acceptable for a bid set if the intent (allowance vs. later selection) is clear.

**Issue: TBD colors without allowance clarification.**

I'm now checking the material abbreviations (SS-1, WD-1, etc.) to verify they're all defined somewhere in the drawings.

**Issue: No drawing legend for material abbreviations** - these codes are explained in specs but should also appear in a legend on the drawings for standalone readability.

Also noticing "Crawlspace" vs "Crawl Space" inconsistency for Room 21 - minor but worth flagging.

I'm spot-checking detail references, like "1/A7.01" on A2.01A, to confirm callouts point to the correct details.

Section cuts also need alignment verification - checking A2.01's "1/A3.10" marker against A3.10's actual longitudinal section, which appears to match.

The specs reference optimizing "electrical primary wiring for high load circuits" but the actual load calculations, panel schedule, and circuit assignments needed to verify this aren't included in the drawing set.

**Cross-discipline references:**

Structural notes appropriately point to "SEE STRUCTURAL SET" for foundation and framing items outside architectural scope - A2.00 correctly references "SEE STRUCTURAL SET FOR PIER AND BEAM FOUNDATION". But coordination items like beam/column locations affecting interior layouts, foundation steps, and cantilevers need cross-checking between disciplines.

Specification callouts are generic ("SEE SPECS") rather than citing specific section numbers like "SEE SPEC SECTION 07 31 13" for roofing.

**Gridline dimensioning:**

G0.01 states partitions at gridlines are located by "face of framing... at the grid" - but doesn't specify which face (interior vs. exterior), which could cause ambiguity. Flagging this as an issue.

**Scale notation:**

Sheets include graphic scales, which is good practice, though some details are marked "NTS" (not to scale), indicating schematic-only representation.

**Coordination notes:**

"COORDINATE WITH ARCHITECT" and "VERIFY IN FIELD" notes appear appropriately for field conditions - like the PV/solar penetration on A2.01B. The set doesn't show excessive VIF notes, so this seems reasonable rather than indicating incomplete design.

**Lighting fixture schedule:**

A6.01's RCP includes a lighting fixture schedule with types L1, L3-L9 listed.

**Issue found:** The schedule lists Description and Count but omits manufacturer/model, lamp type/wattage, voltage, and mounting type - all shown as TBD, which is acceptable for a bid set where fixtures get finalized later.

**Door swing indication:**

The door schedule doesn't note handing (left/right-hand swing), though plans show swings graphically as standard practice. Adding handing to the schedule would help with ordering clarity.

**Floor drain details:**

A2.01A shows "FD" symbols at multiple locations, but drain type, size, grate style, and drainage connection aren't detailed.

**Issue found:** Floor drain specs missing (type, size, grate, rough-in location).

**Reflected ceiling plan symbols:**

RCP A6.01 uses symbols (L1, L3, C, etc.) referencing a lighting legend, but "C" for Cat6E data locations isn't defined directly on the RCP sheet - only in the notes section elsewhere.

**Supply and return grilles:**

A2.01A shows "SG" and "RG" for HVAC, but these don't appear on the RCP where ceiling diffusers would typically be shown. This suggests they might be wall or floor-mounted rather than ceiling-mounted.

Checking the keynotes confirms it: SG is called out as "FLUSH IN FLOOR WOOD SUPPLY GRILLE - MATCH FLOORING," so these are floor grilles - explaining their absence from the RCP.

**General notes:**

G0.01 covers dimensioning standards, but the set lacks a comprehensive general notes sheet addressing construction standards, substitution procedures, contractor responsibilities, submittal requirements, and quality control. These might live in the specs, but having them on the drawings aids field reference.

**Product data sheets:**

Specs call out specific products (Andersen windows, Delta fixtures, Thermory wood) without indicating whether data sheets exist elsewhere in the project manual.

For a bid set, product data often comes later, but contractors still need clarity on whether substitutions are allowed. The specs lack a clear substitution policy.

**Issue found:** No product substitution policy or procedures included.

**Special inspections:**

Beyond standard code inspections, nothing addresses testing like blower door tests, HVAC commissioning, or insulation verification. The specs mention "Built to HERO code" with certification "tbd" but don't detail what testing HERO certification requires.

**Issue found:** Special inspections/testing not specified for energy code or HERO certification verification.

**Allowances:**

The specs list several allowances, including door levers as black metal hardware.

Other allowances: entry door handleset (Level Lock or similar), septic system, well system, and various TBD finishes/selections. None of these include dollar amounts, which contractors need for bidding.

**Issue found:** Allowances identified but dollar amounts missing.

**Project schedule:**

No overall schedule, milestones, or completion date appear anywhere - these would typically be in front-end documents or the contract itself.

**As-built requirements:**

Nothing about as-built drawings, record documents, or closeout submittals.

**Warranty information:**

No warranty periods specified for roofing, appliances, windows, or other components.

That covers all seven categories thoroughly. Time to compile the findings list.

Let me double-check my notes before finalizing to make sure nothing's missed, then format everything as required.

The Bonfire House drawing set and specifications represent a comprehensive residential design package with strong architectural intent and modern energy-efficient features. The documents would benefit from a thorough coordination review focusing on dimensional completeness, code compliance verification information, and building envelope detailing before issuing for construction.
